NET-1.title: Read Bittensor identity safely without adding chain writes
NET-1.what: Build a small read-only boundary that turns one exact network and metagraph observation into Carbon-owned wallet, hotkey, and UID associations.
NET-1.why: UIDs can disappear or be reassigned and provider responses can fail. Carbon must bind identity to the observed network snapshot instead of treating chain state as timeless scientific truth.
NET-1.changes: Carbon gains a deterministic, testable way to read and classify network identity while keeping the Bittensor SDK inside the chain adapter.
NET-1.not_yet: This does not authenticate application requests, bind candidates, load keys, sign transactions, publish weights, run localnet, contact a live chain in tests, or qualify network security or production use.

NET-2.title: Verify who sent each request and prevent replay
NET-2.what: Wrap SDK btauth/1 and the unchanged seven-tool MCP core with contextual messages and a bounded durable replay journal.
NET-2.why: A hotkey signature must remain bound to the exact network, challenge, snapshot and request without becoming scientific authority.
NET-2.changes: Canonical v1 ingress, SDK signatures, durable nonce/request receipts, identity and time watermarks, and precise bounded failures.
NET-2.not_yet: No evaluator, accepted flag, public listener, public deployment, weight publication, scientific/security qualification or LIVE authority.

NET-3.title: Bind each candidate to its artifact and original author
NET-3.what: Retain canonical Strategy artifacts and original authenticated receipts, then compose A7 admission, A8 fixture evaluation and A6 publication.
NET-3.why: Commitment must not create scientific merit; copies and wallet changes must not create fresh evaluation or improvement identity.
NET-3.changes: Bounded durable commitments and fixture accepted records with exact scientific score bytes, immutable context and explicit interrupted-dispatch state.
NET-3.not_yet: No real scientific acceptance, second evaluator, arbitrary execution, hidden disclosure, weight publication, localnet success or LIVE authority.

C-REWARD.title: Reward accepted improvements and preserve the unearned share
C-REWARD.what: Register accepted baselines, immutable allocation and funding terms; close authenticated batches and persist improvement credit with finalized-chain age.
C-REWARD.why: Reward targets must preserve scientific authority, copied-artifact identity, restart age and every challenge allocation.
C-REWARD.changes: Q12 floor/remainder reward ledger, shared-holder aggregation, burn-only targets, weekly review and A6 aliased scorecard.
C-REWARD.not_yet: No real scientific qualification, signing, runtime burn proof, treasury deployment, public transaction, economic optimality or LIVE claim.

NET-4A.title: Nominal publication intents
NET-4A.what: Issue nominal localnet references backed by immutable reward projections and the existing journal.
NET-4A.why: Fixture results and caller flags must never acquire public-testnet or treasury authority.
NET-4A.changes: Context-bound validity, supersession, changed-state/quarantine checks and explicit no-winner burn intents.
NET-4A.not_yet: No SDK signing, runtime burn proof, public transaction, treasury deployment, science/security qualification or LIVE authority.

NET-4B.title: Verified complete-vector publication and recovery
NET-4B.what: Compile complete reward targets against fresh identity/runtime capabilities and journal guarded SDK dispatch, finality, reveal and readback.
NET-4B.why: A valid preview can be rebuilt at execute time; ambiguous dispatch and stale stored weights cannot be treated as cleared payouts.
NET-4B.changes: Pinned runtime burn checks, explicit quantization tolerance, final SDK integer/call guards, durable transaction identity and heartbeat/recovery.
NET-4B.not_yet: No actual localnet burn/epoch proof, public transaction, treasury deployment, scientific/security qualification or G2/LIVE authority.

NET-5.title: Reproducible disposable localnet integration
NET-5.what: Reproduce the complete fixture-to-chain path and collect actual runtime identity, rows, epochs and recovery evidence.
NET-5.why: Unit contracts and source pins cannot prove chain effects, burn behavior or local operation.
NET-5.changes: An isolated pinned-image runner, guarded local setup, three fixed synthetic exam identities and actual SDK/chain integration tests.
NET-5.not_yet: No C1 scientific evidence, public network, treasury, security qualification or automatic G2 readiness.

NET-6.title: Disposable operator lifecycle and recovery
NET-6.what: Explicit configuration, external keys, exclusive process ownership, health and consistent private backup/restore.
NET-6.why: A tested publication function needs honest lifecycle and recovery controls before local operation can be reproduced.
NET-6.changes: Guarded operator CLI, retained private configuration, restart-safe node startup, bounded health, OS lease and no-overwrite restore.
NET-6.not_yet: No public operation, treasury, real scientific archive, production custody or G2 readiness claim.

C-01.title: Keep scientific attempts durable without duplicate execution
C-01.what: Persist the exact A7 attempt, scientific and environment bindings before dispatch, then retain partial work and opaque result associations across restart.
C-01.why: A crash must not silently rerun a Strategy, resample protected evaluation or erase completed work.
C-01.changes: C1 gains atomic queue claims, explicit restart reconciliation, exact retry continuity and requester-safe status.
C-01.not_yet: No reconstruction, score, signed receipt, archive acknowledgement, publication, chain activity, scientific qualification or LIVE authority.

C-AUTH1.title: Turn structured scientific goals into a verified Burgers package
C-AUTH1.what: Import the supplied typed authoring contracts and exact Burgers Dynamics V1 development package into Carbon's existing owners.
C-AUTH1.why: Authors need deterministic, reviewable package construction without copying a second scheduler or bypassing scientific governance.
C-AUTH1.changes: C1 gains a closed content-addressed goal compiler, exact 12-cell public-development generator, separated TRAIN/EVAL/STRESS plan and explicit reference/JAX/archive handoffs.
C-AUTH1.not_yet: The public workbench cases are not a protected exam, accepted baseline, qualified reference, durable archive acknowledgement or testnet evidence.

C-EA0.title: Define when evaluation evidence is actually captured and durable
C-EA0.what: Specify attempt coverage, required artifacts, custody zones, retention classes, completeness, named uses and durability acknowledgement using existing result owners.
C-EA0.why: A stored result reference is not enough to prove that required evidence survived, is usable for its named purpose or may be finalized.
C-EA0.changes: C1 gains an exact versioned documentation contract and machine-checkable cases for immutable attempt accounting, five independent status axes, explicit missingness/dependence/unknowns and positive acknowledgement conditions.
C-EA0.not_yet: This does not implement an archive, invent retention or legal policy, acknowledge durability, set science, qualify evidence, deploy infrastructure or authorize a network.

C-EA1.title: Implement durable evidence only after its policies are approved
C-EA1.what: Implement a versioned archive catalogue, immutable artifacts, verified manifests, stage journal, transactional outbox and positive availability acknowledgement.
C-EA1.why: A real result cannot finalize safely until required evidence is preserved and verified under an approved durability and custody model.
C-EA1.changes: Nothing yet; the implementation ticket remains unstarted and input-blocked.
C-EA1.not_yet: No database, object store, key system, deployment, retention policy, security qualification, archive acknowledgement or finalization integration exists.
